sections.overview: The Blue-capped Rock Thrush is a migratory Old World flycatcher that breeds in the Himalayas and winters farther south in the Indian subcontinent.
sections.identification: The male has a blue head, orange-rufous rump and underparts, a dark mask and a conspicuous white wing patch. Females are browner and more subdued.
sections.habitat: It breeds in open or pine forest and rocky, grassy Himalayan hills, generally at montane elevations; winter habitat includes wooded areas farther south.
sections.diet: It feeds mainly on invertebrates, taken on or near the ground.
sections.behavior: During winter it can move with mixed-species flocks; in the breeding season males sing from exposed perches.
sections.reproduction: It breeds in the Himalayan region; available species summaries report a clutch of roughly three to four eggs.
sections.ecology: Despite its English name, it is a forest-associated flycatcher rather than a true thrush; it belongs to Muscicapidae.
sections.conservation: The global assessment is Least Concern, while the State of India’s Birds reports a declining national trend; these assessments describe different geographic scales.
